question: Does uniform vector scaling remove joint-error direction distortion, and do causal early-query opportunities exist under a trace-derived positive threshold?
authority: User requests one small experiment and supervisor paper within one hour; user confirms this machine and saved traces.
scope: Offline development diagnostic, no new physical comparison or optimizer search.

donors.exposure: All four historical tasks are exposed development evidence; none is a new recovery audit.

geometry.episodes: all 24 verified full Part2/3 recordings, engineering excluded
geometry.bounds: recorded action-space bounds after adaptation; low-level actuator output limits are not replayed

timing.common_cap_choice: Original free-motion cap and recovery-plan domain; fixed before scoring, no outcome selection.
timing.eligible_chunks: Only factual complete eight-action prefixes; each restarts at its actual query. Discard incomplete final prefixes and four-action schedules.
timing.quantile_method: linear, over strictly positive accumulated eligible-prefix correction values on calibration episodes only
timing.selected_threshold: median positive eligible correction; if absent, omit positive-threshold timing gene
timing.counterfactual_scope: First would-trigger age within a recorded factual prefix only. Stop interpretation there. No refreshed VLA proposals or changed-state trajectories are inferred.
timing.claim: Opportunity counts are replay diagnostics, not realized new query costs or safe completion.

budget.task_horizon: No original episode is truncated or relabelled.

limitations: Joint-space direction preservation is an algebraic property, not an uprightness or collision guarantee.
Counterfactual commands are evaluated only at factual measured joints; physical effects require a later matched simulator screen.
Threshold calibration uses correlated prefixes from only two tasks; task denominators remain explicit.
No result is used to claim evolution beats random search or ordinary learning.
